corrections.issue: Wrong speaker: the inflation study and the statement that trend following does well in high and rising inflation are Neils (referring to a study done at Dunn), not Katie.
corrections.fix: Neils Kostrup Larsen: Trend following performs well in high and rising inflation, according to a long study of inflation and trend following.

corrections.issue: Wrong speaker: the 2000-2019 worst period and the Dunn track-record comparison (referring to a Dunn track record) are Neils, not Katie.
corrections.fix: Neils Kostrup Larsen: The worst CTA period was 2000 to 2019 with low and stable inflation, while the Dunn track record compounded fastest in 1982 to 2000 with relatively low but unstable inflation, so instability matters more than level.

corrections.issue: Mixed speakers: price being the pure truth and data manipulation are Neils, but the point that economic-trend signals are weakened by missing official data is Katie.
corrections.fix: Neils: price data is the pure signal, official data can be delayed or manipulated. Katie: an economic-trend strategy is weakened when official data are missing.

completeness_estimate: 0.80 - first reader captured most numeric and strategic points but missed several mechanism steps (inflation turbulence mechanism, shock-duration logic, AQR response-lag rationale, no-significance caveat), sector colour and mis-attributed two inflation claims to Katie instead of Neils
